title: Kan-fibration criterion for homotopy-cartesian squares
statement: Use small simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and homotopy-cartesian squares in the two-leg fibration-replacement sense specified in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition], and Kan fibrations from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Let $a:Q\to X$, $b:Q\to Y$, $f:X\to Z$, $g:Y\to Z$ be simplicial maps satisfying $fa=gb$. Suppose $g$ is a Kan fibration. Then the square is homotopy cartesian if and only if its canonical map $Q\to X\times_ZY$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No Kan-complex or nonemptiness assumption on $Q,X,Y,Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 2.3 and Lemma 2.5 with its right-properness proof, printed p.4: strict-pullback comparison for a cospan with one fibration leg. The arbitrary-base extension agrees with the Kan path model by lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy theorem.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_ZY$ and let $c:Q\to P$ have coordinates $(a,b)$. The model factorization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] gives $X\xrightarrow{i}X_f\xrightarrow{p}Z$ with $i$ a weak equivalence and $p$ a Kan fibration. Set $P_f=X_f\times_ZY$, and write $h:P_f\to X_f$ for the first projection. This projection is a Kan fibration directly from the horn lifting definition: lift the prescribed $Z$-simplex through $g$, retaining the already prescribed $X_f$-simplex. The square with top $d:P\to P_f$, $d(x,y)=(i(x),y)$, bottom $i:X\to X_f$, and vertical first projections is a strict pullback. Indeed $P_f\times_{X_f}X$ consists degreewise of $((x_f,y),x)$ with $x_f=i(x)$ and $p(x_f)=g(y)$; eliminating $x_f$ gives exactly $f(x)=g(y)$. These mutually inverse coordinate formulas commute with faces and degeneracies. Hence $d$ is the pullback of the weak equivalence $i$ along the Kan fibration $h$, and right properness in the cited core theorem makes $d$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Section 2.3 and proof of Lemma 2.5, printed p.4; agent expansion of the comparison with arbitrary two-leg replacement witnesses. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Suppose $c$ is a weak equivalence. The composite $dc:Q\to P_f$ has coordinates $(ia,b)$, and is a weak equivalence by the model two-out-of-three axiom of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. Use the factorization of $f$ from step 1 and the factorization $Y\xrightarrow{1_Y}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ of $g$. The latter is allowed because $1_Y$ is a weak equivalence and $g$ is a Kan fibration by hypothesis. Their two-leg replacement pullback is exactly $P_f$, and their induced map is $dc$. Thus the defining existential condition for homotopy cartesianness in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition] holds.

source.place: Section 2.3 and proof of Lemma 2.5, printed p.4; agent expansion of the comparison with arbitrary two-leg replacement witnesses. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely suppose the square is homotopy cartesian. Its definition in [lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition] supplies factorizations $X\xrightarrow{u}\widehat X\xrightarrow{\widehat f}Z$ and $Y\xrightarrow{v}\widehat Y\xrightarrow{\widehat g}Z$, where $u,v$ are weak equivalences, $\widehat f,\widehat g$ are Kan fibrations, $\widehat f u=f$, $\widehat g v=g$, and $w:Q\to\widehat X\times_Z\widehat Y$, $w(q)=(ua(q),vb(q))$, is a weak equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] to the cospans $Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xleftarrow{f}X$ and $\widehat Y\xrightarrow{\widehat g}Z\xleftarrow{\widehat f}\widehat X$, with its three vertical maps $\alpha=v$, $\beta=1_Z$, $\gamma=u$. They are weak equivalences and the two required equalities are precisely the factorization equalities. Its two fibration hypotheses concern $g$ and $\widehat g$, which hold; it requires no fibrancy of any object. Its conclusion says that $e:P\to\widehat X\times_Z\widehat Y$, $e(x,y)=(u(x),v(y))$, is a weak equivalence, after swapping the two coordinates of both pullbacks. Coordinate swap is a simplicial isomorphism; its realization is a homeomorphism and hence a weak equivalence. Degreewise $ec=w$, since both coordinates are $(ua,vb)$. The model two-out-of-three axiom in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] applied to $e$ and $ec$ therefore makes $c$ a weak equivalence, proving the converse.

The delivery has no new nodes, and the statement, unit and blueprint ancestry are unchanged. Step 1: factor f=p∘i (MC5 of lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core); I checked degreewise that P_f×_{X_f}X=P, so d=(i,1) is the base change of i along the Kan fibration h, and right properness (last sentence of the core node) makes d a weak equivalence. Step 2: the witnesses (i,p) and (1_Y,g) are allowed by the defining clause of lem-coef-kan-fibrant-path-recognition, and the induced map is dc=(ia,b). Step 3: lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance applies to the cospans Y→Z←X and Ŷ→Z←X̂ with α=v, β=1_Z, γ=u. Its Kan legs are g and ĝ, and its equalities are the factorization equalities. After the coordinate swaps, ec=w, and two-out-of-three gives c a weak equivalence. The weak-equivalence notions of def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones and the core node agree. Edge cases checked: empty Z or Y, Z=Y=Δ^0, and arbitrary non-Kan bases. The Kan hypothesis on g is necessary: Δ^0 at vertex 0 and Δ^0 at vertex 1 over Δ^1 give an empty strict pullback but a contractible homotopy pullback, and the item keeps that hypothesis. The one citer, lem-coef-sharp-pullback-calculus, uses exactly this statement. All dependencies are in the same unit, so there are no tool_uses. No SGA source is cited. Rezk §2.3/Lemma 2.5 is not archived (WANTED) and I did not fetch it. lean.statement: theorem kan_homotopy_cartesian_fibration_criterion {Q X Y Z : SSet.{u}} (a : Q ⟶ X) (b : Q ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : a ≫ f = b ≫ g) [Fibration g] : (∃ (Xf Yf : SSet.{u}) (i : X ⟶ Xf) (j : Y ⟶ Yf) (ff : Xf ⟶ Z) (gf : Yf ⟶ Z), i ≫ ff = f ∧ j ≫ gf = g ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence i ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence j ∧ Fibration ff ∧ Fibration gf ∧ ∃ c : Q ⟶ pullback ff gf, c ≫ pullback.fst ff gf = a ≫ i ∧ c ≫ pullback.snd ff gf = b ≫ j ∧ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence c) ↔ IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (pullback.lift a b h)
lean.note: Expands the identical two-leg replacement condition from kan_fibrant_path_recognition; uses pullback.lift for the canonical strict comparison. No Kan or nonemptiness hypotheses on the objects. Does not import the downstream SharpPullbackCalculus module.
